correctness.rationale: Exact equivalence of separation and coverage predicates to bit-union criteria on a fully specified fourteen-vertex twenty-one-edge graph; all 6,476 subsets of cardinality up to six are considered, ruling out any smaller solution. Two independent Fano-plane encodings and exhaustive scripts agree on 168 five-edge-resolving bases all missing precisely one ve-covered edge, on 1,386 joint six-bases, their 574/672/84/56 five-base containment profile, 17,514 jump edges and 5,040 slide edges. The cyclic-incidence verifier separately exhaustively confirms 11 automorphism orbits. Full BFS from all 1,386 states determines connectivity, radii and diameters 6/6 and 7/9, respectively. Both executables were replayed from embedded package paths. Limits: finite exact theorem only; two codepaths are not an external scholarly audit.

value.rationale: A natural simultaneous edge-separation and radius-one edge-coverage optimization from a 2022 definition is evaluated exactly on the canonical 3-regular Fano incidence network. Its optimum increases by exactly one landmark over known edge-metric bases; every old optimum fails coverage at exactly one edge. The 1,386 optimal combined sensor layouts include 574 not formed by adjoining a sensor to any old edge-metric basis. Their local one-token movement nevertheless connects all minima, contrasting with the 21 disconnected eight-cycles for five-landmark edge-only optima, and has exact radius 7, diameter 9 and eleven symmetry classes. This is a motivated finite classification useful for benchmarking constrained sensor replacement; no unproved all-order theorem or downstream application is asserted.
